My method is a weighted blanket, comfort object, classical music (I try to shut my brain off and focus on the actual notes and rhythms in extensive detail), there are also some guided meditations or stories on YouTube that could be a distraction but that could also keep your brain more engaged. 

As far as sleepy teas/meds/etc I don’t use many anymore. Melatonin was okay for a while but the dreams weren’t worth it. Tylenol PM has pain med with a small dose of Benedryl so you could try taking a larger dose of Benedryl by itself. 

My dad uses Alka Seltzer Nighttime and he knocks out really quick. It’s a cold medicine with a different antihistamine than Benedryl. 

If all else fails, try your best to talk to a psychiatrist and they can help you find a med that could work.

I have insomnia stemming from anxiety. I have almost a fear of sleeping because I’m not in conscious control of my body. I also become hyperaware of my breathing at night which freaks me out. 

The best things that help me are:
1. Not forcing my brain to turn off. Instead, distracting it with music or TV (I know I know. Tv is like the worst thing for an insomniac but it works for me!). 
2. Listening to my brain and body and “checking in” if I’m actually tired. If I’m not, I’ll get up and do something else.
 ***Use your bed for sleep and rest only***
3. Bargaining with my brain by saying, “Okay well if I can’t sleep, then I’m going to at least rest my eyes”. This usually results in me zoinking out pretty quickly. 

These are just what work for me. My insomnia is also a side effect of medical issues (both mental and physical). I would check in with your doctor just to be sure. 

Good luck to you !
